en: In the city of Kapila, the Bodhisattva Śrī Siddhārtha, having abandoned his queen together with their son, as well as all his wealth and the glory of a universal monarch,
on the full moon night of the month of Āṣāḍha at midnight, with a mind turned toward renunciation—
Bearing the status of a śramaṇa, he went forth, desiring to seek liberation. // Yaśo_1 //
Then at dawn, Queen Yaśodharā, having risen from her bed together with her son,
set out in haste out of a desire to see her noble lord.
Not far away was the bedchamber. // Yaśas 2 //
Just as in the past he had hidden my husband somewhere in secret to deceive me,
she thoroughly searched the interior and exterior of the palace.
Even though she examined him, she did not see him at all.
Therefore, out of grief, she ran very swiftly to the minister’s house, flung open the window,
and struck the door firmly again and again.
Being concealed, he cried out repeatedly, "I am here! I am here! // Yaśo_4 //
Looking toward something within the house,
she stood for a moment near the doorkeeper; then, her breath coming in gasps due to the interruption of her reflection, she touched her chest with her hand.
He struck his pair of cheeks. // Yaśo_5 //
Then she went to the king’s stable,
but she did not see the horse Kanthaka there; where had that beloved one gone, and why did he depart in such haste?
As she was reflecting thus, she fell into a swoon. // Yaśo_6 //
Reflecting on something or other,
she moved her head here and there and struck her son’s face with the two eyes [of her face] under the parasol of her arms.
She checked [the flow], with droplets of falling tears.
Unable to endure at all the intense surge of mental anguish, with her pride greatly wounded,
[she cast down] the jeweled necklace given by her husband.
Also a garland of coral and a pair of earrings. // Yaśo_8 //
Having removed her forehead ornament, her golden ring, her girdle bound with a gold thread, her head-jewel, and her bracelets;
Uttering "Fie! Fie! in agitation, she released [the arrow]. (Yaśas 9)
He struck the ground with the soles of his feet; he yawned and pulled upward at his hair;
and he uttered confused words devoid of meaning.
She cried out like one terrified and wept with a faltering voice. (Yaśas 10)
Having laid the child upon the bed, she repeatedly lifted him up with both hands at once,
shaking his head as if she were unconscious.
He roared, he sighed, he fell down, and he writhed in agony. // Yaśo_11 //
Though constantly tormented by hunger,
she did not desire to eat anything at all; though afflicted by thirst, she did not take even a single drop of water.
And as he drank, a trembling also arose within his body. // Yaśo_12 //
Intelligence, memory, power, and fortitude are destroyed;
the complexion of the body and strength, as well as the faculties of the senses,
perish, and life itself gradually comes to an end.
In the end, there is this: separation from what is dear. (Yaśas 13)
Sitting on the ground with her body bent in half, she placed her head and both hands upon her lap; then, slightly bending her neck, she remained there.
Today, I have taken refuge in the ocean of anxiety. (Yaśas 14)
Unable to endure the act of dishonor toward Yaśodharā, Prince Siddhārtha went alone to the forest, having abandoned his dwelling.
"Ah, may such a reputation also belong to me! (Yaśas 15)
Whatever task there was in the three palaces, the capable servant performed it accordingly; whether he had gone out, was standing still, or was lying down, she never did anything displeasing.
At no time did I ever do anything whatsoever.
Reflecting upon the sudden calamity that had befallen her beloved,
she approached the temple of the deity with fragrant flowers, incense, and lamps.
He reverently honored the host of gods. // Yaśo_17 //
Placing both arms upon her head, the grieving woman gazed at the splendor of the face of the divine image;
having bowed with devotion and a completely purified heart, she paid homage.
"By which [means] he entreated the gods," thus [it is said] because of separation. // Yaśo_18 //
The gods— Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva— are the causes of the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the three worlds;
they are the lords of the universe, possessed of great majesty.
May they be my refuge, for I am in great suffering. // Yaśo_19 //
Having thus made his request, he placed the two farmers as an offering in the hands of the gods and bound them; meanwhile,
he presented sweet new water and milk-rice.
A white garment and a golden statuette. // Yaśas 20 //
He caused the lords of the gods to experience great joy by sounding the bells,
and he had the brahmins recite hymns of praise in the divine language.
She bowed down repeatedly, prostrating herself upon the ground.
"Let them look with divine vision for which dwelling— even in a pure forest— he would be happy to live,
and having found such a home, let them turn him back."
She was sought again by the denizens of heaven as they yearned for her.
Gazing with a sidelong, unblinking eye,
she firmly planted her foot upon the surface of the earth, repeatedly biting her tender lower lip.
Having raised and shaken [his hand], he brandished his index finger. // Yaśo_23 //
"Have you not heard of the noble one’s departure from his home? Have you not seen it? Tell me, why are you so unperturbed? Thus the doorkeeper spoke loudly in anger.
With tears in her eyes, she questioned him with a loud cry. (Yaśas 24)
O noble lady, that crest-jewel of the royal lineage was not seen by me when he arrived at the gate accompanied by excellent women in the pleasure grove.
"I have heard that she took her pleasure with him when night had fallen. (Yaśas 25)
Surely the prince was not free from passion; for did he not desire a new beloved from him?
Having privately married some woman, he composed a certain short play.
"I am going outside," thus do I reflect. (Yaśas 26)
For in the past, the highly illustrious Mandhātṛ,
though a universal monarch, abandoned human women out of his passion for the throngs of celestial nymphs.
He indeed attained the splendor of the city of the gods.
Leaving behind the host of celestial beauties who are pleasing to the mind,
he embraced the female ascetic, the wife of Agastya, in the hermitage of the ascetics in the Vindhya forest.
The subduer of Pāka dallied with her at night. // Yaśo_28 //
Having conquered Laṅkā, the foremost king, the ten-faced Rāvaṇa went to the Daṇḍaka forest,
even after seizing Sītā, the daughter of Janaka.
He made that [world] his own, just like his own beloved wife. // Yaśas 29 //
And in former times, Maheśvara, while performing austerities with his queen Umā in the Kali forest,
set aside the cultivation of continuous meditative absorption.
And indeed, she brought forth two sons. // Yaśo_30 //
"Thus, in order to console that most excellent bride who was overwhelmed with grief,
the doorkeeper, out of compassion, placed his joined palms upon his chest and spoke in a sweet voice."
With his head bowed, he made his request with these words.
Have you seen the Blessed One anywhere now—
whether at home, outside, or even in a grove—
at the break of day or during the night?
Thus he questioned his own female servant with anger. (Yaśas 32)
Placing her right knee and both arms upon the ground, with her forehead touching her head and her body bent low, the servant spoke.
And there is nothing that I do not know, whether heard or seen.
After this, having ascended the palace and wiped the tears of moisture from her eyes, she thought:
"Oh, has my noble husband arrived here or not?"
He questioned the eunuch who was the guardian of the inner apartments.
With their praiseworthy forms, their lovely speech, their splendor, and their composure, they have come to your presence;
O most exalted one, honored by all people.
He has three beloved wives. // Yaśo_35 //
Bhavatī, Bhāratī, and likewise Lakṣmī— these beloved women are delightful to the mind;
with them, the young prince always delights.
May his mind never at any time take delight elsewhere.
Is it because your husband has turned away from those desires which are loathed by wise and noble men and are fraught with faults,
that he has never once visited the inner apartments?
Neither heard nor seen, neither by day nor by night. // Yaśo_37 //
Having attained equanimity toward those whose wealth is asceticism, he would find no pleasure anywhere in the three worlds,
regarding his own harem as equal to a house filled with impurities.
How does this husband of yours take his pleasure? (Yaśas 38)
In this abode of incurable diseases, where happiness is absent and the stomach is perpetually tormented by hunger,
it cannot be satiated by various kinds of food and drink.
The wise man does not conceive a longing for the body. // Yaśo_39 //
Beholding the body— its skin dappled with scattered droplets of perspiration and its surface defiled by various stains of filth— a person is brought to ruin.
Like a moth [flying] toward the brilliant radiance of a lamp's flame. // Yaśo_40 //
Then Yaśodharā, giving close attention to the words spoken by the guardian of the king’s inner apartments,
[beheld] that place which was like the Nandana grove of the gods.
He went to the royal grove with a restless mind. // Yaśas 41 //
Then the guardian of the delightful grove,
stepping forward with his hands folded upon his chest,
asked: "Noble lady, for what purpose have you come here?"
"I have come desiring to know," he announced.
"Friend, has my noble lord arrived here in secret at dawn,
or has he not? Have you seen him here, or have you heard of him?"
Having reflected thoroughly, speak to me according to reality.
Free from longing for the five objects of sensual desire, that noble son would have his senses conquered;
thereafter, he would come together with the delightful grove.
Neither have I seen it, O Noble One, nor indeed have I heard of it.
Desiring to bring about the prosperity of the inhabitants of the three worlds,
he descended from heaven by his own meritorious splendor after receiving the request of the gods.
That Lord was born in a human birth. // Yaśo_45 //
Having reflected upon the cause of this, "Why has the sage Asita gone to heaven during this great festival?",
he [the Bodhisattva] considered himself the son of King Śuddhodana, his own friend.
"Janī," she said, and out of joy she went to see him. (Yaśas 46)
Then the sage Asita, having arrived at the king’s palace, beheld the prince, who was endowed with a wealth of merit,
by means of his eye consisting of supramundane knowledge.
Examining the characteristics of his body, // Yaśas_47 //
The child spoke these words: "This one shall indeed become a meritorious Buddha, having destroyed the bonds of Māra;
he will lead across all men, gods, and asuras."
"From the great ocean of saṃsāra, which has no further shore. (Yaśo 48)
Then, having examined the physical characteristics of the five twice-born ones, the wise Kauṇḍinya said:
"This child, having destroyed the impurities of thirst and the like..."
He shall go to the unsurpassed state of a Buddha. // Yaśo_49 //
Then, at the very moment of his birth, as he walked upon the heads of seven lotuses in the Lumbinī grove,
he let out a fearless roar that resounded throughout the three worlds.
"May I become the foremost," [he thought], like a lion cub. (Yaśo_50)
With its sweet sound made pleasant by the humming of wandering bees,
fragrant with heaps of floral pollen,
and possessing winds mingled with the spray of ripples;
Then, a gentle breeze blew slowly throughout the forest from all sides. // Yaśo_51 //
At the birth of that Great-Souled One, the most excellent, the treasures of the earth emerged;
then the lady Earth rejoiced exceedingly.
He displayed on earth an accomplishment that inspired wonder. // Yaśo_52 //
Thereafter, from the Lumbinī grove, those two parents, full of affection, [brought] the young prince to their home, which resembled a variegated image of Jāmbūnada gold.
Having surrounded him along with his circle of kinsmen, they led him away.

Favored by his guru, he shall, through the power of the merit accumulated in birth after birth, receive according to the prescribed rite the entire system of knowledge and its observances, as well as the philosophical vision, from his guru.
This wise one has attained meditative concentration without long delay.
Indeed, in the sixteenth year from the birth of this noble son— who has attained the splendor of fresh youth through learning and fortitude— it shall be together with you.
He duly performed the marriage consecration according to the prescribed rites.
